newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaica brewery boss wins palimony appeal.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica brewery boss wins palimony appeal.

text.p: An appeals court overturned a landmark "palimony" ruling that would have forced business tycoon Paul Geddes to hand over a portion of his estate to his estranged lover, a newspaper reported on Thursday.

The court on Wednesday overturned a lower court ruling two years ago that Geddes, chairman of the Desnoes & Geddes brewery, should give one-sixth of his assets to hotelier Helga Stoeckert, his common-law wife for 32 years, the Jamaica Observer said.

Stoeckert, 65, lived with Geddes, 84, until 1991, when Geddes sent her belongings to her hotel in a moving van. He married a Caymanian hotel manager in her 30s one week later and Stoeckert sued, claiming half of Geddes's estate as compensation for the business and other assistance she said she had provided him.

When the lower court ruled that Stoeckert deserved one-sixth of Geddes's assets, legal experts said the case could have repercussions for thousands of common-law relationships in the Caribbean nation.
Geddes, son of a founder of the brewery that makes Jamaica's famed Red Stripe beer, appealed the ruling, as did Stoeckert, who still claimed one half.

The appeals court found that Stoeckert had benefited "significantly" from the relationship with Geddes and in fact was seeking "compensation for the pain and agony which she experienced in seeing her lover abandon her for a much younger woman," the Observer reported.
Stoeckert, who left then East Germany as a refugee and owns the Four Seasons Hotel in Kingston, has vowed to appeal the case to the British privy council.
